FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:775](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L775) defines `J(A)` with monetary, latency, and balance terms, but [dynamic_management.py:900](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L900) chooses candidates only by current load fraction and [dynamic_management.py:912](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L912) never consults `c_m` or `tau_m`. The heuristic therefore does not optimize the advertised objective except by accident. Reproduced: with two idle admissible models where one is 1000x more expensive and much slower, the solver still assigns the task to the first-listed expensive model (`[[1, 0]]`) because the load-fraction tie preserves list order.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Score each tentative assignment by incremental objective delta `ΔJ` and pick the minimum-feasible placement; at minimum, tie-break equal load fractions using `c_m` and `tau_m` instead of list order.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:943](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L943) checks feasibility, but [dynamic_management.py:947](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L947) reduces HARD-constraint violations to `warnings.warn(...)` and [dynamic_management.py:956](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L956) still returns a normal `(Allocation, cost, balanced)` tuple. [dynamic_management.py:3226](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3226) forwards that tuple unchanged from `DynamicManager.get_allocation()`. This means invalid allocations are not part of the type contract; callers must notice a warning side-channel or they will dispatch infeasible plans as if they were valid.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make infeasibility explicit in the return contract by returning `(allocation, cost, balanced, feasible, violations)` or by raising on any HARD-constraint breach; `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` should refuse to hand back infeasible plans.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:285](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L285) and [dynamic_management.py:304](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L304) do not enforce unique `model_id` or `task_id`. [dynamic_management.py:736](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L736) silently collapses duplicate IDs into dict keys, while [dynamic_management.py:661](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L661), [dynamic_management.py:670](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L670), and [dynamic_management.py:680](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L680) then resolve by first match or overwrite in `task_map`. Reproduced: two tasks both named `"same"` with loads 1000 and 5000 yield matrix `[[1],[1]]`, but `model_load('m', ...)` returns `10000` instead of `6000` because both rows map to the second task object. Duplicate model IDs are equally ambiguous for accessors and role lookup.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate uniqueness of all `task_id` and `model_id` values at construction time in `LoadBalancer` and `Allocation`, and fail fast on duplicates.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:694](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L694) correctly treats positive load on `L <= 0` as infinite load fraction in `Allocation.model_load_fraction()`, but [dynamic_management.py:800](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L800) and [dynamic_management.py:860](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L860) coerce the same case to `0.0` inside `_objective()` and `_balanced()`. Combined with forced assignment at [dynamic_management.py:917](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L917), a zero-capacity model can receive work while the cost model reports no bottleneck penalty and the balance predicate can still return `True`. Reproduced: one model with `L=0` and one 1000-token task yields `balanced=True`, while the accessor reports `inf` load fraction and feasibility reports F1 overload.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use a single definition of load fraction everywhere: if `L <= 0` and load is positive, propagate `inf` or mark the allocation infeasible immediately; do not let `_objective()` or `_balanced()` treat that case as zero load.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:1022](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1022) claims `validate_k1()` checks both universal assignment and feasibility `sum b_j <= L1`, but the implementation only checks that column 0 is populated. Because the solver force-assigns overloads, the validator still reports success on impossible K=1 allocations. [dynamic_management.py:1041](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1041) reduces the homogeneous proof to `balanced`, yet `_balanced()` is so lax under the default threshold that even a skew matrix placing all three tasks on one PAR still returns `True`. These helpers therefore give false confidence in the claimed reduction properties.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `validate_k1()` assert actual feasibility, and make `validate_homogeneous()` compare the achieved distribution against an expected equal-split tolerance across admissible workers rather than reusing the public `balanced` predicate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
